quiz.q: Which one do you need to compile Hello.java with javac?
quiz.explain: Only the JDK contains javac. The JRE and the JVM can only run compiled bytecode.

options: The JVM plus the standard class library
quiz.explain: JRE = JVM + class library: everything you need to run a program, nothing to compile one.

quiz.q: What does this print when you run it with JDK 25?
quiz.explain: java.class.version is the bytecode version the JVM supports: 69.0 for Java 25 (67.0 for Java 23).

quiz.q: You compile with JDK 25 and start the .class with JDK 23. What happens?
quiz.explain: An older JVM cannot run newer bytecode. The other way round works: JDK 25 runs JDK 23 bytecode.

options: No: feature is a method and needs brackets
quiz.explain: javac reports "cannot find symbol: variable feature". Write Runtime.version().feature().
An unknown property name is not an error: getProperty returns null. Check the spelling: java.version.

quiz.q: What does "write once, run anywhere" mean?
options: One JVM runs on every operating system
The same bytecode runs on any JVM of the same or a newer version, on any OS
quiz.explain: The bytecode is portable. The JVM itself is built separately for Windows, macOS and Linux.

quiz.q: Which statement about Java 25 is true?
options: It is a short release, like Java 23
It is an LTS release; java -version shows LTS
It brought back a separate JRE from Oracle
Its JVM can no longer run Java 23 bytecode
quiz.explain: Java 25 is LTS. There is still no separate Oracle JRE, and a newer JVM always runs older bytecode.

quiz.q: java Hello.java works on a full JDK. Why does it fail on a runtime that has only java.base?
options: The launcher compiles in memory and needs jdk.compiler
quiz.explain: Single-file launch compiles the source first. Without the jdk.compiler module the launcher stops with "Module jdk.compiler not in boot Layer".

flashcards.back: It runs bytecode: loads classes, interprets, JIT-compiles hot code, manages memory.
The JVM plus the standard class library.

flashcards.front: What does the JDK add to the JRE?
flashcards.back: Development tools: javac, jshell, jar, javadoc, jlink.

flashcards.front: Which part do you need to compile Java code?
flashcards.back: The JDK: only it has javac.

flashcards.front: Is the JVM the same program on every operating system?
flashcards.back: No. There is a JVM per OS; the bytecode is the same.
Bytecode, plus the class file version that made it.

flashcards.front: Can a Java 25 JVM run Java 23 bytecode?
flashcards.back: Yes. Newer JVMs run older bytecode.

flashcards.front: Which error do you get when an older JVM meets newer bytecode?
Does Oracle still ship a separate JRE?
flashcards.back: No, not since JDK 11. Some vendors do; jlink builds your own.
